primary.title: AI auditors catch most agent misbehavior but flood reviewers with false alarms, new study finds
primary.summary: AI models can often spot problematic behavior by other AI agents in logs, according to a study by Anthropic researcher Andy Hall. GPT-5 found about 98 percent of reward-hacking cases, but the more exhaustively the search is tuned, the more false alarms pile up. That's not yet enough for reliable safety checks. The article AI auditors catch most agent misbehavior but flood reviewers with false alarms, new study finds appeared first on The Decoder.

primary.title: State propaganda in some Chinese AI models is only "a thin layer" that fine-tuning can strip away
primary.summary: Nous Research retrained Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B to produce Arete-27B, largely stripping out its pro-Chinese bias. The propaganda rate dropped from 22 percent to less than one percent, while general capabilities remained intact in tests. The method relied on 53 million tokens of supervised fine-tuning. The political bias is "applied late, it is applied thin," the team writes. primary.title: Open Source pg_vectorsearch Brings More Scalable Vector Search to PostgreSQL
primary.summary: Tiger Data has released pg_vectorsearch, an open source PostgreSQL extension for vector similarity search, currently in alpha. Its PRISM index uses data partitioning and compression instead of the graph-based approach used by pgvector’s HNSW index, reducing memory requirements and index build times. By Renato Losio
